findings.message: The pass marker is read from a path that can already hold a committed value. Nothing removes or resets `.specclaw/features/$FLEET_CHANGE/integration-result` before `run_agent`. A leftover `pass` from an earlier integration, carried in by the feature branch, is read as this run's result. 'The agent did not write a result' then reads as 'verified', which is the defect the fix was meant to close. Delete the marker (and `git rm` it if tracked) before the agent starts, or compare it against a per-run nonce. Add a test where a stale `pass` exists and the agent writes nothing.
findings.scenario: A prior integration run committed `integration-result` = pass, and it ended up on feature/<m> or main. After a new member merge, the integrate pod runs, the agent exits 0 without touching the file, and `integration_passed` sees the old `pass`. The pod sets FLEET_PR_DRAFT=false and opens or publishes a ready-for-review 'integration verified' PR into the trusted branch.

findings.message: The test for the KUBECONFIG/.env fix cannot fail without the fix. The second command in `pl` is `bash -c 'echo kc=[${KUBECONFIG-unset}]'`, a fresh shell that never runs the fleet binary. It always prints `unset` whether or not `load_local_env` is skipped. The first command only keeps `doctor | head -1`, which is unlikely to contain the committed `evil` value. Run a real fleet command under TF_BUILD and capture the KUBECONFIG and context the binary itself ends up with, for example a debug or dry-run subcommand that prints them. Cover both variables and also FLEET_TRUSTED_CONFIG.
findings.scenario: Remove the `TF_BUILD` guard in bin/specclaw-fleet. `.specclaw/.env` is then loaded and KUBECONFIG points to evil-kubeconfig. The test still passes: the bash -c subshell prints `unset`, and doctor's first line has no `evil`.

findings.message: The unreadable-PR-search fix has a single-variant test (`SEARCH_JUNK`, an HTML body). B2 requires the named case plus at least two others. Add variants for an empty body, a JSON object without `.value` (for example an error `{"message":...}`), `{"value":null}` and a non-array `.value`. Each must produce no PR POST.
findings.scenario: A regression that only checks for HTML, or an `id` check that accepts `{"message":"TF401019"}`, still passes the single test while a JSON error body creates a duplicate PR.

findings.message: The PR target is now decided in two places that can disagree. The entrypoint exports SPECCLAW_PR_TARGET only for feature/* refs or an explicit FLEET_PR_TARGET, so ordinary agent PRs follow git.base_branch. The pod's fallback in `ensure_pr` uses `${SPECCLAW_PR_TARGET:-$FLEET_REF}` and ignores git.base_branch. Make the fallback use the same resolution as specclaw-azdo-pr, or leave the target unset and skip the fallback.
findings.scenario: git.base_branch=develop and FLEET_REF=main with no FLEET_PR_TARGET. When the agent opens a PR itself, it targets develop. When the agent fails and the pod creates the fallback draft, it targets main. The same change gets different targets depending on who opened the PR.
